replies.content: Memory spikes are often a lagging indicator of a churn-driven CPU bottleneck. If the user_id label turns over every few minutes, the Prometheus process spends more cycles on head block compaction and index re-indexing than on scrape ingestion. The issue isn't just the 3-4KB footprint per series. Write amplification spikes during block compaction when new series arrive and old ones expire. To catch this early, monitor the rate of series churn against the scrape interval. If churn exceeds 10% of total cardinality per hour, compaction pressure will likely trigger a memory spike before you hit the actual cardinality limit.
